Rasulullaah ﷺ then made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Forgive the Ansaar, the children of the Ansaar and the grandchildren of the Ansaar." Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ also asked Allaah to forgive the spouses of the Ansaar. Yet another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Allaah! Forgive the Ansaar, the children of the Ansaar, the grandchildren of the Ansaar and their neighbours."
sources: Bazzaar and Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.40) has commented on the chain of narrators.
Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.4l) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Another report mentions that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Allaah! Forgive the Ansaar, the children of the Ansaar and the friends of the Ansaar."

Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) narrates that he heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, "Imaan belongs to Yemen and in the progeny of Qahtaan (an ancient king to whose progeny belongs all the people of Yemen as well as the Ansaar). Hard-heartedness is to be found amongst the progeny of Adnaan whereas in the Himyar tribe is the commander and leader of the Arabs. While the Madh'hij tribe is the chief and defence of the Arabs and the Azd tribe is their shoulders and head (bearing the weight of important matters), the Hamdaan tribe is their crest and their summit. O Allaah! Give honour to the Ansaar through whom Allaah established the Deen; who gave me shelter, who assisted me and who gave me their undaunted support. They are my companions in this world, shall be my party in the Aakhirah and the first of my Ummah to enter Jannah."
sources: Bazzaar, narrating from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.41).

paras: Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Muhammad ﷺ narrates that in one of his sermons, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) related the relationship between the Muhaajireen and the Ansaar to the poem that states: "May Allaah reward ja'far (the Ansaar) on our behalf Who helped us when our shoes made us slip and fall in the path of those who ( 1 ) Ahmad (Vol .3 Pg. 1 39) . Haythami has commented on the narration. wished to trample us They refused to become frustrated with us (through times) that even our mothers Would become frustrated with us, were our mothers to suffer what they (the Ansaar) suffered because ofus"
sources: Ibn Abi Dunya in Ashraaf, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.7 Pg.134). -

paras: What Rasulullaah ﷺ said about the Quraysh Hadhrat Humayd bin Abdur Rahmaan Himyari narrates that when Rasulullaah passed away, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was at one end of Madinah (where he lived). When he arrived, he opened the face of Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "May my parents be sacrificed for you! You are so pure in life and death. I swear by the Rabb of the Kabah that Muhammad ﷺ has indeed passed away." (When he heard that the Ansaar had gathered to discuss the Khilaafah,) Hadhrat Abu Bakr followed by Hadhrat Umar (RA) went to the Ansaar. In his talk to the Ansaar, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) did not omit to mention any verse of the Qur'aan or statement of Rasulullaah ﷺ concerning the virtues of the Ansaar. He also said, "I am also aware that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'If everyone walks a valley and the Ansaar walk another valley, I shall walk the valley of the Ansaar.' O Sa'd Because you were sitting there, you know that Rasulullaah said, 'The Quraysh are the successors of this matter (Khilaafah). Righteous people will follow the righteous of the Quraysh while sinful people will follow the sinful of the Quraysh." Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) confirmed this when he said to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), "You have spoken the truth, we shall be viziers while you are the leaders."
sources: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA), one of the leaders of the Ansaar.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) narrates that after Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, several speakers from the Ansaar delivered lectures (in the orchard of the Banu Saa'idah tribe where the Muhaajireen and the Ansaar had gathered to discuss the Khilaafah). One of them said, "O assembly of Muhaajireen! Whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ appointed one of you to a post, he would also put one of us with him. We therefore feel that two persons should take this post, one from us and one from you." The other speakers from the Ansaar followed suit until Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) stood up and said, "Since Rasulullaah ﷺ was from amongst the Muhaajireen, the leader should be from the Muhaajireen. We shall be his Ansaar (helpers) just as we were the Ansaar (helpers) of Rasulullaah Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then stood up and said, "O Assembly of Ansaar! May Allaah reward you all tremendously. May Allaah keep this speaker of yours steadfast. By Allaah! Should you do otherwise (other than what Hadhfat Zaid has mentioned), we would not reconcile with you." Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit then took hold of the hand of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and said, "This is the man. Pledge your allegiance to him."
sources: Tayaalisi, ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg. 151), Ibn Abi Shayba, Bayhaqi (Vol.8 Pg.134) and others, as quoted in Kanzul Pg.131). Haythami (Vol.5 Pg.183) says that Tabraani and Ahmad have also reported the narration from reliable sources. Tabraani has also reported a similar narration from Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA), as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg. 1 40).

paras: Hadhrat Qaasim bin Muhammad narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, the Ansaar gathered around Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA). Hadhrat Abu Bakr, Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah also arrived there. Hadhrat Hubaab bin Mundhir (RA) who had participated in the Battle of Badr stood up and said, "One leader from you (Muhaajireen) and one from us (Ansaar). O honoured group (of Muhaajireen)! I swear by Allaah that we do not begrudge you this position but we fear that such a person may become the leader whose fathers or brothers we (Ansaar) may have killed (when fighting for islaam. He should then not wish to take revenge from us)." Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "If it ever happens, you should rather die (fighting him) if you are able to."

Hadhrat Abu Bakr il then started to speak. He said, "We shall be the leaders while you be the viziers. This matter will be shared equally between us just as the frond of a date palm divides at the centre." The first person to pledge his allegiance was Hadhrat Basheer bin Sa'd (also known as) Abu Nu'maan. After everyone had united under the leadership of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), an occasion arrived when he had to distribute some wealth amongst the people. He sent Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) to an old lady from the Banu Adi bin Najaar tribe with her share of the wealth, when she askeu what it was, Hadhrat Zaid told her that it was her share of the wealth that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) had given to the women. She remarked, "Do you wish to bribe me away from my Deen?" "Certainly not," replied Hadhrat Zaid (RA). She then asked, "Do you fear that I shall leave the Deen I follow?" "Definitely not," responded Hadhrat Zaid She then said, "I swear by Allaah that I shall never accept anything from him in future." When Hadhrat Zaid (RA) returned and informed Hadhrat Abu Bakr about what the old lady had expressed, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "We shall also not take back anything that we have given her."
sources: Ibn Sa'd and Ibn Jareer, as quoted in Kanzul Pg.130).
